atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.group_play_line: Use the same short phrases while two children share one favorite toy.
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.instructions: Share a favorite toy and model 'my turn' and 'your turn' when the toy changes hands. Pause briefly before passing it so the child has an opportunity to use the phrase. Keep the exchange quick and playful.
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.make_easier: Model the whole phrase and immediately give the child the turn. A single word or gesture is also accepted and expanded aloud.
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.make_harder: Model one extra word naturally, such as 'my turn please,' without requiring it.
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.materials: a favorite shared toy, simple game, blocks, cars, or another play item
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.success_criteria: The child attempts 'my turn,' 'your turn,' or another meaningful two-word turn-taking phrase.
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.title: My Turn
atpl1:01cdd9f34e37a62bed4feda4300902a7.what_to_avoid: Do not take away a toy simply to force speech or require repeated imitation before giving the child a turn.

atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.group_play_line: One person can ask for more before the next person gets the bubbles.
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.instructions: Play for a few turns, then pause before starting again. Model a short phrase such as 'more bubbles' and wait a few seconds. Accept a close attempt, then immediately continue the activity. Repeat naturally for 3-5 opportunities.
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.make_easier: Accept one word and expand it aloud. If the child says 'bubbles,' respond with 'more bubbles' and continue right away.
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.make_harder: Offer two choices and model a specific two-word request for the preferred item.
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.materials: bubbles or another favorite repeatable toy
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.success_criteria: The child attempts a meaningful two-word request such as 'more bubbles' or 'more please.'
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.title: More Bubbles
atpl1:041794bbb1acb1f86a27ca9460088c2d.what_to_avoid: Do not repeatedly demand the phrase or withhold the activity while waiting for perfect speech.

atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.group_play_line: Read the same book with a sibling and let each name one object.
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.instructions: Use the same book each day this week. Point to the same two or three objects and ask 'What's this?' Pause for an attempt, then name it. Familiarity makes naming easier, so repetition is the point.
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.make_easier: Ask about only one object per sitting.
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.make_harder: Add one new object to the set.
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.materials: one favourite book the child already knows
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.success_criteria: The child names a familiar pictured object more readily than earlier in the week.
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.title: Same Book, Every Day
atpl1:06a431b9e9a8e118a900b7f407fecc02.what_to_avoid: Do not swap books mid-week in search of novelty.

atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.group_play_line: Each child points to one thing per page and names it.
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.instructions: Let the child turn the pages and point to whatever interests them. When they point, ask 'What's this?' and wait. Follow their lead rather than your own page order.
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.make_easier: Name what they pointed at and invite them to say it with you.
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.make_harder: Ask one follow-up, such as 'What colour is it?'
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.success_criteria: The child points to an object of their own choosing and attempts to name it.
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.title: Point and Tell
atpl1:1081de288d8fc18f41225d80bb291a63.what_to_avoid: Do not redirect the child to the object you wanted to practise.

atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.group_play_line: During shared play, model respecting another person's 'all done' or 'please stop.'
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.instructions: During play or a routine, model short phrases the child can use to finish, refuse, or pause something, such as 'all done,' 'no more,' or 'please stop.' When the child communicates that they are finished, respond promptly so they learn that their communication has meaning.
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.make_easier: Accept a gesture or one word such as 'stop' or 'done,' then model the two-word version without requiring repetition.
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.make_harder: Model a slightly longer functional phrase such as 'I'm all done,' 'I need break,' or 'please stop now' without making the longer phrase mandatory.
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.materials: an ordinary play activity or daily routine
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.success_criteria: The child attempts a two-word phrase to stop, finish, refuse, or set a boundary.
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.title: All Done and Stop
atpl1:1226e454bd64d869206574bb6ad9851f.what_to_avoid: Never ignore a clear 'stop,' 'no,' or 'all done' merely to get a longer phrase.

atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.group_play_line: Two children take turns choosing a colour and painting one mark each.
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.instructions: Put 2–3 colour jars in front of your child. Model choosing: 'red paint!' and dip a finger. Hold the jars slightly back and wait. When your child reaches, model: 'blue paint!' and let them choose. Do 4–5 colour choices, celebrating each two-word attempt.
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.make_easier: Name the colour first and wait for any response before giving access.
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.make_harder: Put the paint jars out of reach — your child must request before painting.
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.materials: 2–3 small jars of finger paint or paint chips, a piece of paper
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.success_criteria: Your child uses a colour word plus 'paint' or 'want' in any order.
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.title: Paint Choice Words
atpl1:13a4fd9b1e557d877381cc41fed5098c.what_to_avoid: Avoid correcting colour names mid-activity — any two-word attempt is a win.

atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.group_play_line: Let two people choose different items and model a short request for each choice.
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.instructions: Show two choices and name them simply. Ask which one the child wants. When the child reaches, points, looks, or says a word, model a two-word phrase such as 'want car' or 'want book.' Pause briefly, then give the chosen item.
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.make_easier: Accept the item name alone and expand it aloud, such as 'car' to 'want car.'
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.make_harder: Model one additional word naturally, such as 'I want car,' without requiring the longer phrase.
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.materials: two preferred toys, books, snacks, or activities
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.success_criteria: The child attempts a two-word request combining 'want' with the chosen item.
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.title: Want + Choice
atpl1:166c4e5492dab00d41b9fb4d5162202b.what_to_avoid: Do not make access to food, comfort, or essential items depend on producing the phrase.

atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.group_play_line: With another child, one holds the toys and the other chooses each round.
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.instructions: Hold one toy in each hand. Say 'which one?' and wait. If your child reaches or looks, say the name and give it. Try again with a different pair. Do 3-4 choices.
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.make_easier: Hold out just one toy and wait for any reach or vocalization.
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.make_harder: Hold toys out of reach and wait for your child to use a word or sign.
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.materials: two favourite toys your child knows
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.success_criteria: Your child communicates a choice (reach, point, word, or sound).
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.title: Pick Your Toy
atpl1:2a9316b59bfcfef283cfeeb26a2034f6.what_to_avoid: Avoid giving the toy before any communication attempt.

atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.group_play_line: Let another person set up a scene and describe it in a short sentence.
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.instructions: Act out a simple scene with two familiar figures and model a short sentence naming who, the action, and the object, such as 'Dog eats the food' or 'Baby drinks milk.' Pause before acting so the child can try the sentence.
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.make_easier: Use the same scene repeatedly and model the sentence before each action.
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.make_harder: Change one element and model the new sentence during the same play.
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.materials: toy animals, dolls, toy cars, or familiar play figures
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word sentence combining a subject, an action, and an object.
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.title: Who Is Doing What
atpl1:2c317105a4151f55be1d2122a16fc3fc.what_to_avoid: Do not correct word order when the meaning is already clear.

atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.group_play_line: Two children take turns, one pointing and one naming.
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.instructions: Sit together and open to a clear page. Point to one object and ask 'What's this?' Wait about five seconds. Accept any word attempt, then say the name clearly once and turn the page. Do 5-6 pages.
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.make_easier: Name the object yourself first, then point again and ask.
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.make_harder: Ask about a smaller detail on a busier page.
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.materials: a picture book with clear single objects, one per page
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.success_criteria: The child attempts to name at least two pictured objects.
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.theme: naming objects in a familiar book
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.title: What's on This Page?
atpl1:3550b9ec30305b58d9cbbaa24c58e5b2.what_to_avoid: Do not turn the page before waiting the full five seconds.

atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.group_play_line: Two children take turns asking for more during a shared snack or game.
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.instructions: Give your child a very small piece of snack or a brief turn with a toy. When it runs out, wait silently and look expectant. If your child reaches, points, or makes a sound, say 'more!' and model it. Wait for any attempt — a sound, approximation, or gesture — then give more. Do 4-5 turns. Try pairing a gesture: hold up one finger for 'more.'
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.make_easier: Hold the item in your hand and wait for any reach — give it immediately.
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.make_harder: Wait for 'more' plus a word: 'more cracker', modelling the two words together.
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.materials: a favourite snack, toy, or activity in small amounts
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.success_criteria: Your child communicates 'more' using any word, sound, sign, or gesture.
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.title: More Please Routine
atpl1:3b00aee6c8a322cddda1ec55543158a2.what_to_avoid: Avoid giving more before any communication attempt — the wait is what builds the habit.

atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.group_play_line: Two children each request one item — take turns being the one who holds the tray.
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.instructions: Put 2–3 objects on a tray between you and your child. Hold one up and say 'want cracker?' then wait. If your child reaches or sounds, model the two words: 'want cracker!' Give it over immediately. Repeat with other objects, modelling 'want ball,' 'open box.' Do 4–5 turns.
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.make_easier: Accept one word plus a reach — say the two-word phrase yourself and give the item.
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.make_harder: Wait for a two-word phrase before handing over the item.
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.materials: 2–3 small familiar objects (cracker, ball, box) on a tray
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.success_criteria: Your child uses any two-word combination or approximation to request an item.
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.title: Two-Word Choice Game
atpl1:5e054d694dcf6b0e700951eb4c2ebe8d.what_to_avoid: Avoid asking 'say want cracker' — model the phrase and wait.

atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.group_play_line: Have another familiar person model 'help me' naturally during shared play.
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.instructions: Choose something the child enjoys and may naturally need a little help with. When the child shows they need assistance, model 'help me.' Pause briefly for an attempt, then help right away.
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.make_easier: Respond to any clear request for help and expand a single word aloud, such as 'help' to 'help me.'
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.make_harder: Model a more specific short request such as 'help open' or 'help please.'
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.materials: a toy container, zipper, puzzle, jar, wind-up toy, or another safe task where help may naturally be useful
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.success_criteria: The child attempts a two-word help request such as 'help me' or 'help please.'
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.title: Help Me
atpl1:5f44b9eba107589ca26c6610f2c6cb05.what_to_avoid: Do not intentionally frustrate the child, create unsafe obstacles, or withhold needed help to elicit speech.

atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.group_play_line: Model respecting another person's request for a break during shared play.
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.instructions: During an activity, model short sentences the child can use to pause or stop, such as 'I need a break' or 'All done now.' When the child communicates this, respond promptly so they learn the words work.
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.make_easier: Accept 'break,' 'done,' or a gesture and model the fuller sentence once.
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.make_harder: Model 'I need a break please' without requiring the extra word.
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.materials: an ordinary play activity or daily routine
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word phrase to pause, stop, or finish.
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.title: I Need a Break
atpl1:797708a5514fd175e24bf0bac3f2a8ff.what_to_avoid: Never ignore a clear request to stop in order to get a longer sentence.

atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.group_play_line: Two children each name one snack per round and share the choosing.
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.instructions: Put two snacks on the table. Name each one slowly: 'cracker… banana.' Ask 'which one?' and wait 5 seconds. Give the chosen snack and name it as you hand it over. Repeat for 3-4 choices.
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.make_easier: Put only one snack on the table and wait for any reach or sound before handing it over.
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.make_harder: Cover the snacks and ask your child to name one from memory before you uncover it.
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.materials: two small snacks your child likes
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.success_criteria: Your child indicates a snack choice through any means (point, word, reach, or eye gaze).
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.title: Snack Choice Words
atpl1:7e97ac6a60c3623f7a609c1c2b7e1995.what_to_avoid: Avoid handing the snack before your child has made any communicative attempt.

atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.group_play_line: Two children take turns hiding an object for the other to find.
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.instructions: Put 4-5 objects on the table and name each one together. Ask your child to close or cover their eyes. Remove one object and hide it in the box. Say 'open your eyes — what's missing?' Wait for any attempt — a point, word, or sound.
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.make_easier: Use only 2 objects so the missing one is obvious.
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.make_harder: Use 6 objects and remove two at once.
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.materials: a shoe box or bag, 4-5 small familiar objects
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.success_criteria: Your child notices something is gone and attempts to name or indicate the missing object.
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.title: What's Missing? Box
atpl1:80d40c4226b091fc36ba73aeb061651e.what_to_avoid: Avoid removing the object before your child has had a chance to name all the objects first.

atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.group_play_line: Two children take turns pointing: one points, the other names.
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.instructions: Open the book to a clear picture. Point and ask 'what's that?' Wait 5 seconds. Accept any sound, word, or point. Say the name clearly once and turn the page. Do 5-6 pages.
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.make_easier: Name the picture yourself first, then go back and ask again.
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.make_harder: Ask 'where is the [item]?' and wait for your child to point on a busy page.
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.materials: a picture book with clear single objects on each page
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.success_criteria: Your child attempts to name or point to at least 2 pictured items.
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.title: What's That? Book
atpl1:987acefca5dcf8001c218aba7a951022.what_to_avoid: Avoid moving past a page before waiting the full 5 seconds.

atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.group_play_line: Another familiar person models the same request during shared play.
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.instructions: Offer something the child wants that needs opening. When they bring it to you, model 'Help me open.' Pause briefly, then open it right away.
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.make_easier: Accept 'help' or 'open' and expand it aloud once.
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.make_harder: Model naming the object too, such as 'Help me open box.'
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.materials: a container with a lid, a zipped bag, a jar, or a wrapped snack
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.success_criteria: The child attempts a three-word request naming the help needed, such as 'help me open.'
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.title: Help Me Open
atpl1:9b0facf380b755262eadbf9d76820e7a.what_to_avoid: Do not create difficult or unsafe containers, or delay help to extend practice.

atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.group_play_line: Each person takes a turn asking for the activity in their own words.
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.instructions: Play for a turn, then pause and model a short sentence such as 'I want bubbles.' Wait a few seconds and accept any closer attempt, then continue right away. Offer 3-5 natural openings during the activity.
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.make_easier: Accept a two-word version such as 'want bubbles' and expand it aloud once.
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.make_harder: Model a slightly fuller sentence such as 'I want more bubbles' without requiring it.
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.materials: bubbles, a wind-up toy, or another favorite repeatable activity
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word request such as 'I want bubbles.'
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.title: I Want Bubbles
atpl1:9b9eb883a67400556702486fc177e75b.what_to_avoid: Do not withhold the activity while waiting for the full sentence.

atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.group_play_line: Take turns asking to join each other's play.
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.instructions: Start playing with something inviting. When the child shows interest, model 'Can I play?' and pause briefly. Welcome them in immediately after any attempt.
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.make_easier: Accept 'play' or a gesture and expand it aloud.
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.make_harder: Model 'Can I play too?' without requiring the extra word.
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.materials: a shared game, blocks, or any activity already underway
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.success_criteria: The child attempts a short question such as 'Can I play?' to join an activity.
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.title: Can I Play?
atpl1:9e165d6d242e3e887ddb32f6d7c48486.what_to_avoid: Do not exclude the child from play to prompt the phrase.

atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.group_play_line: Two children take turns — one names the item, the other picks it up.
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.instructions: Scatter toys on the floor. Say '[item] in the basket!' and wait for your child to pick it up and drop it in. After each success, name the next item. Do 4-5 cleanup requests. Keep the instructions simple: one item at a time.
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.make_easier: Point to the item as you name it and hold the basket close.
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.make_harder: Name 2 items in one instruction: 'ball and cup in the basket!'
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.materials: 5-8 small toys on the floor, a basket
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.success_criteria: Your child picks up and places at least 2 named items into the basket.
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.title: Cleanup Request Game
atpl1:aa5d7da84faba502ab7a4c6284f1347d.what_to_avoid: Avoid naming all items at once — one clear instruction at a time.

atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.group_play_line: Two children take turns guessing who is in each photo.
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.instructions: Show one photo at a time. Ask 'who is this?' and wait 5 seconds. Accept any sound, word, or point. Say the name clearly: 'That's grandma!' and show the next photo. Do 4-5 photos per round.
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.make_easier: Name the person first, then show the photo again and wait for any response.
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.make_harder: Mix in a photo of an unfamiliar person and see if your child says 'don't know.'
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.materials: 3-5 photos of familiar family members on your phone or printed
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.success_criteria: Your child attempts to name or point to at least two people in the photos.
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.title: Family Photo Names
atpl1:adafba440db93934b88a2fa45a364f1d.what_to_avoid: Avoid correcting close attempts — 'dada' for daddy is a great start.

atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.group_play_line: Let one child lift while the other names.
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.instructions: Cover or close a flap over one object. Say 'What's under here?' and lift it together. Pause for an attempt, then name it clearly. Do four or five reveals.
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.make_easier: Lift the flap first, then ask for the name.
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.make_harder: Ask the child to guess before lifting.
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.materials: a lift-the-flap book, or a book with a cloth laid over part of the page
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.success_criteria: The child attempts to name the revealed object.
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.title: Lift the Flap, Name It
atpl1:bd6a98e7eef7d1a01c1e48baa8230317.what_to_avoid: Do not hold the flap shut while waiting for a word.

atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.group_play_line: Two children use the same phrase while sharing one toy.
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.instructions: Pass a favorite toy back and forth. Model 'My turn please' before you take it and pause before passing it so the child has an opening. Keep each turn short.
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.make_easier: Accept 'my turn' and expand it aloud without requiring repetition.
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.make_harder: Model 'Can I have a turn?' without making the longer form mandatory.
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.materials: one favorite shared toy or a simple turn-taking game
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.success_criteria: The child attempts a three-word turn-taking phrase such as 'my turn please.'
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.title: My Turn Please
atpl1:c694ec43189c20633adeea5502833f6b.what_to_avoid: Do not withhold a turn until the phrase is produced correctly.

atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.group_play_line: Two children take turns: one asks, the other gives the object.
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.instructions: Lay out four objects in a row. Point to two and name them slowly: 'spoon… ball.' Ask 'can you give me the spoon?' and wait 5 seconds. If correct, celebrate and put it in a basket. Try all four objects across 2-3 rounds.
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.make_easier: Use only two objects and give a visual cue (point gently toward the correct one).
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.make_harder: Ask for two objects in one request: 'give me the cup AND the ball.'
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.materials: four small familiar objects (spoon, block, ball, cup)
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.success_criteria: Your child gives you the named object at least twice.
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.title: Give Me Two! Game
atpl1:ca49a944bb6b1181d845524845bdb023.what_to_avoid: Avoid pointing to the correct object immediately — wait the full 5 seconds first.

atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.group_play_line: Two children walk together — one points, the other names.
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.instructions: Walk slowly around one room with your child. Stop at an object, tap it, and ask 'what's this?' Wait 5 seconds. Accept any sound, point, or word. Name it and move on. Visit 5-6 objects per walk.
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.make_easier: Name the object first, then visit it again and ask 'what's this?'
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.make_harder: Ask 'what do we do with this?' for each object to practise function words.
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.materials: no materials needed — walk around one room
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.success_criteria: Your child attempts to name or respond to at least 3 objects on the walk.
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.title: Quick Naming Walk
atpl1:cb95176fdcc5cff557bdc409da186304.what_to_avoid: Avoid asking about the same object twice in one walk.

atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.group_play_line: One child finds while the other names, then swap.
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.instructions: Choose a page with several familiar objects. Say 'Can you find the cup?' and wait. When the child points, ask 'What's this?' and give them a moment to name it. Repeat with three or four objects.
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.make_easier: Point near the object yourself, then ask for the name.
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.make_harder: Ask the child to find two objects before naming either.
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.materials: a familiar picture book or a simple picture card set
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.success_criteria: The child locates an object and attempts to name it.
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.title: Find and Name
atpl1:e22a325977fbaaeca903a6ea909d17d0.what_to_avoid: Do not correct a close attempt; repeat the clear name once and move on.

atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.group_play_line: Two children take turns: one starts the line, the other fills in the last word.
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.instructions: Start a familiar song together. Slow down and stop just before the last word of a line. Look at your child and wait 3 seconds. Accept any sound, word, or just a look — then finish the word together. Do 4-5 pauses across the song.
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.make_easier: Pause at the very last sound of a word (e.g. 'twin-kle twin-kle little…') and wait.
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.make_harder: Pause mid-song without slowing down — see if your child notices and fills in.
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.materials: a simple song your child knows (e.g. Twinkle Twinkle, Old MacDonald)
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.success_criteria: Your child fills in, attempts, or reacts to at least one pause.
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.title: Song Fill-In Game
atpl1:f273cccd0afd3c96730215bc49ba8096.what_to_avoid: Avoid filling in immediately — the 3-second wait is the key.

atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.group_play_line: Let another person choose an object and model a short action phrase for it.
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.instructions: Choose a simple action with a familiar object and model a short combination such as 'push car,' 'feed bear,' 'wash doll,' or 'open box.' Pause before doing the action and give the child a chance to attempt the two-word combination.
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.make_easier: Use one predictable combination repeatedly during the activity and model it before each action.
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.make_harder: Change the object or action and model a new two-word combination during the same play routine.
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.materials: toy cars, toy animals, blocks, toy food, or other familiar play objects
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.success_criteria: The child attempts a meaningful two-word combination containing an action and an object or person.
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.theme: combining an action with an object
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.title: Action + Object
atpl1:f7a99d017c398560058379637732ac58.what_to_avoid: Do not repeatedly correct word order when the child's two words clearly communicate the intended meaning.

atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.group_play_line: Pass the album and take turns naming one thing each.
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.instructions: Look at photos together. Point to one clear object - a cup, a ball, a dog - and ask 'What's this?' Wait, accept any attempt, and say the name clearly once.
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.make_easier: Offer a choice: 'Is this a ball or a cup?'
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.make_harder: Ask the child to find an object you name before asking them to name another.
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.materials: printed family photos or photos on a phone showing clear single objects
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.success_criteria: The child attempts to name at least two objects in the photos.
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.title: Photo Album Names
atpl1:f83b5f3cd8ef75cdba82700d6b389be7.what_to_avoid: Do not move quickly through many photos; two or three is enough.
